                "Topic": "B.071 zero-based budgeting rationale",
                "MicroTopic": "zero-based budgeting rationale",
                "UniqueConceptKey": "B-071-zero-based-budgeting-rationale",
                "LOSTag": "B.1 Budgeting concepts and strategic planning",
                "Difficulty": "Easy",
                "ItemType": "MCQ",
                "ItemStyle": "single-select",
                "Stem": "Vantage requires every department to justify its entire budget from a base of zero each year rather than starting from the prior year's figures. What is the main advantage of this zero-based budgeting approach?",
                "Choices": {
                        "A": "It is faster to prepare than incremental budgeting",
                        "B": "It prevents any changes to historical spending patterns",
                        "C": "It forces justification of all costs and can eliminate outdated spending",
                        "D": "It automatically increases departmental accountability without added effort"
                },
                "CorrectChoice": "C",
                "ExplanationCorrect": "Zero-based budgeting requires each cost to be justified from zero each period, which helps eliminate spending that persists simply because it existed in prior budgets, though it is typically more time-consuming than incremental budgeting.",
                "StudyLinks": [
                        {
                                "label": "IMA CMA Learning Outcome Statements, Part 1 Section B",

                        },

                        }

                ],
                "ExplanationWrongA": "Zero-based budgeting is notably slower and more resource-intensive than incremental budgeting, not faster. Incremental budgeting starts from prior-period figures and adjusts incrementally; ZBB requires every activity and cost to be justified from a zero base each period, demanding significantly more analysis, documentation, and management time.",
